This knowledge module teaches Joe what FlowJoe is and how a new user gets going — the first-run onboarding, the left-tree/right-gallery mental model, and the local-first and structure-plus-references concepts.

Loading this knowledge is not evidence about which onboarding steps this user completed or how their flow is organized.

## Quick Start & Onboarding

A walkthrough of your first-run welcome wizard and the interactive coach-mark tour in FlowJoe.

When you open FlowJoe for the first time, you are greeted by **Joe**—your local AI assistant. Joe guides you through a brief, two-minute onboarding flow to set up your first workspace and show you around.
Here is what to expect during your first run, and how to get back to those settings later.

**The Welcome Wizard.**
The onboarding wizard helps you seed your project and select your interface preferences.

**Name your Flow.**
Every project starts with a **Flow**—the whole document, containing one or more root nodes. Choose a title that matches your current goal, such as *Novel Draft*, *Research Board*, or *Product Design Plan*.

**Pick a Starting Shape.**
To prevent staring at a blank screen, pick one of our pre-designed outline shapes to seed your tree:
- **Project:** Seeds `Planning`, `Tasks`, and `Assets` nodes.
- **Media Library:** Seeds `Images`, `Audio`, and `Video` nodes.
- **People / Clients:** Seeds `Clients`, `Meetings`, and `Deliverables` nodes.

Also covered in the full docs for this area: Optionally Link Joe AI; Choose a Swatch Theme; The Interactive Coach-Mark Tour; Retours & Customizations.

## Core mental model

Structure, references, and meaning — the three first-class ideas behind every FlowJoe workspace.

FlowJoe is easier once you stop treating it like a folder app or a linear note app. Three ideas do almost all the work.
In the café example, **Brand direction** gives the work a place in the tree. Its gallery holds the visual references. Notes explain the choices behind them.

**Structure.**
A node is not just a label. It is a container that can hold meaning and references.

Also covered in the full docs for this area: References; Meaning; Why keep them separate; Related.

## The two hemispheres

Tree on the left, gallery on the right, and the divider as your control between structure and visual space.

FlowJoe’s main window is deliberately split into structured outlines and media references:

**Left — structure.**
The tree is hierarchical and sequential. It likes order, categorization, parent–child relationships, and knowing where everything belongs.
Use it when you need:
- Project maps and branching plans
- People, chapters, milestones, research threads
- Clear place for a body of work

Also covered in the full docs for this area: Right — references; Choose a different node; The divider; Related.

## Local-first storage

Keep your work close, work offline, and take it with you.

FlowJoe is a desktop workspace that keeps your tree, notes, and imported media on your computer. You can organize ideas and work with saved references without signing into a hosted workspace.

**Work offline.**
Your local outlines, notes, and saved files remain available without an internet connection. Free local audio transcription also works offline after its engine and model are installed.

Also covered in the full docs for this area: Choose how to store a Flow; Keep a portable copy; Choose what leaves your computer.

## Structure · References · Meaning

The core triad that defines every FlowJoe workspace — how order, reference, and intent work together.

Many productivity tools force you into a compromise: you either get a clean text outline with no visual files, or a messy visual canvas where structure is lost.
FlowJoe is designed differently. Every workspace is built around a powerful, unified triad: **Structure**, **References**, and **Meaning**.

**The Triad at a Glance.**
- **Structure** — **The Tree** (Left Hemisphere) — *Where does this live?* — Hierarchy, nesting, task status, visual branch colors

Also covered in the full docs for this area: Structure: The Hierarchy; References: The Media Gallery; Meaning: Intent & Synthesis.
